slides.title: Find pages
slides.body: Pages with many impressions but few clicks are already shown by Google. People often just scroll past them.
slides.action: Export the Search Console Performance report and ask Claude to sort pages by low CTR.
slides.example: “Which pages have 1,000+ impressions but a CTR under 1%?”

slides.title: Rewrite weak
slides.body: Google asks for descriptive, concise titles and warns against boilerplate. Vague titles can get rewritten.
slides.action: Paste each low-CTR page’s title and top query. Ask for 3 unique options per page.
slides.example: “Shop – Page 1” becomes “Women’s Trail Running Shoes | Store Name”.

slides.title: Fix copy-paste
slides.body: Google says identical meta descriptions on every page aren’t helpful. It may use yours for the snippet.
slides.action: Start with the homepage and the most popular pages. One accurate description each.
slides.example: Ask: “Write a description that says what this exact page offers.”

slides.title: Suggest
slides.body: Google finds pages through links. A page that nothing links to can be hard to discover.
slides.action: Give Claude a list of your URLs and titles. Ask which pages should link to one target page.
slides.example: Five guides about running all link to the “Trail running shoes” category.

slides.title: Draft schema,
slides.body: Google recommends JSON-LD for structured data as the easiest format to maintain.
slides.action: Ask for JSON-LD matching only what’s visible on the page. Check it in the Rich Results Test.
slides.example: BreadcrumbList for Home › Running › Trail running shoes.

slides.title: One model,
slides.seed: Always review what an AI writes before it goes live.

slides.body: and I’ll send you a free SEO audit of your site.
slides.sub: Daily SEO and AI search tips.
